description: Default datapath theme: clean monochrome schematic in the spirit of netlistsvg (idea only; geometry drawn fresh for fig-gen). Tokens follow references/CONVENTIONS.md §12. All units are print points. Override per figure (meta.style) or per lab theme (a skin file with the same shape; unspecified keys inherit).

stroke.description: wire: the one stroke weight of every net (data of any bit width, control dashed at the same weight, clock, reset); bit width is shown only by slash-N labels (CONVENTIONS §1, §2.1; net/stroke-uniform). outline: symbol outlines, kept heavier than wires so blocks read before wires.

dash.description: Dash patterns of nets and microarch links scale with stroke.wire (control 3.33× / 2.5× the wire stroke; reset and interrupt 1.33× / 2×; sideband and power ×1.5 of their 0.6 pt originals) so dashes stay readable at the wire weight. boundary and domain_* dash group/chip and domain outlines drawn at stroke.boundary.
dash.microarch_description: stroke.emphasis: emphasized block outline and DMA links; stroke.boundary with dash.boundary: group/chip outlines; dash.domain_*: drawn clock/reset/power domain boundaries; dash.interrupt/sideband/power: microarch link classes.

tokens.junction_description: Junction dot diameter = junction_diam_factor × the net stroke (never below junction_min_diam), so a dot reads as a dot at any wire weight.

arrow.description: One arrowhead size per figure (arrow/nonuniform): about 5.6× the 0.9 pt wire stroke long and 4× wide (the 4.5 × 3.2 pt head of the 0.6 pt wire, scaled); never shortened to fit a short run (arrow/no-room). The layout keeps the last run into a pin at least this long plus route.arrow_min_shaft_pt.

bus_slash.description: Slash-N width mark: length 5 pt (a 10 pt run between layers holds the slash, its number and a full arrowhead), offset from the source, gap to its number.

route.description: jog_min_offset_pt: a data-net level change shorter than this is a redundant jog (error). max_crossings: warning thresholds per net class. crossing_weight: straightening cost of one wire crossing relative to a redundant jog (1000) and a bend (1).

readability.description: Study figures warn (route/readability) when wires cross more than max_crossings_per_net times per drawn net, or run longer than max_wire_length_ratio × the direct distance between their ends. Both are reported for every figure in the receipt (route.readability).

route.straighten_budget_description: straighten_max_evaluations: the straightening search stops after scoring this many candidate layouts per layout plan and keeps the best route found (route/straighten-budget, info). Paper figures need at most about 12 000; large study figures would otherwise take minutes. Deterministic, so a figure always renders the same.
route.arrow_min_shaft_description: arrow_min_shaft_pt: a sink's last run must hold the full arrowhead plus this shaft (0: a head may exactly fill its run, never shortened); the layout moves the riser back (without hugging the upstream block) first, else arrow/no-room.
route.dot_arrow_description: dot_arrow_clearance: minimum distance (pt) from a junction dot center to the base of any arrowhead of the same net and to any pin anchor of the net (route/dot-near-arrow).
route.long_feedback_description: long_feedback_ratio: a returning (backward) branch spanning more than this fraction of the figure width is drawn with named connectors (route/long-feedback). frame_gap_pt: minimum distance of a wire running parallel to a region frame (region/wire-hugs-frame).

elk.min_layer_gap_description: Floor for the gap between layers in tight retries: a width slash, its number and an arrowhead must fit on any wire between two layers (width/missing).
elk.study_description: Study format (one figure sized to content, no column): roomier than 2col (layers 30 pt apart, 8 pt edge/node gaps) so dense RTL analysis figures keep labels off outlines and wires apart without a column-driven spread.

gates.description: Gate-level symbols (AND/OR/XOR/NAND/NOR/XNOR/NOT/BUF, n inputs) drawn from parameters; inverted pins get bubbles (diameter 4 pt, CONVENTIONS §4.1) tangent to the body outline, with the outline stroke. Used for comb gate ops with more than two inputs, inversions, or inside gate-level regions.

join.description: Concatenation (CONVENTIONS §2.3.3): hollow outlined box with the word concat inside on its own middle row; inputs enter on the left, MSB field on top, each labeled just inside the box with its destination bit range in the result.
join.label: concat

split.description: Split (CONVENTIONS §2.3.1): the source bus is a spine; each slice leaves through a 45° ripper stub labeled [msb:lsb]; no junction dot, no body.

op_circle.description: Arithmetic and GF operators drawn as a circle with the operator stroked inside (⊕ GF add/XOR, ⊗ GF multiply, + adder, − subtractor, × multiplier); the glyph is the name, no text.

truncate.description: Truncation (CONVENTIONS §2.3.2): one contiguous range kept is a [msb:lsb] label on the straight wire, no symbol.

extend.description: Sign/zero extension (CONVENTIONS §2.3.4): hollow outlined box with sext or zext, one input, one output.

replicate.description: Replication (CONVENTIONS §2.3.5): hollow outlined box with the words repl ×N ({N} is the count), one input, output N x input width.
replicate.label: repl ×{N}

connector.description: Named off-page connector (CONVENTIONS §1.6): a hollow tag pointing along the flow with the net name inside, drawn in pairs at the source and the sink of a long feedback/return net instead of a loop across the figure.
